title: Sodium-ion battery manufacturing scale-up
bottleneck: Sodium-ion batteries use abundant materials and promise lower costs and better safety than lithium-ion, but energy density is lower and manufacturing exists only at pilot scale. The gigafactories, supply chains, and field data that made lithium-ion cheap do not exist for sodium-ion. Early cells show promise for stationary storage where weight matters less, but bankability requires years of operational data.
why_it_blocks: Sodium-ion could diversify storage away from lithium constraints, but only if manufacturing scales before lithium supply crunches arrive, a race against time with no guaranteed winner.
current_state: Chinese manufacturers are building sodium-ion capacity and early grid pilots are operating. Western manufacturing and long-term performance data are limited. Field data from early deployments will take years to accumulate, during which lithium-ion keeps improving and widening its cost lead.
